steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
I'll systematically investigate the RL training experiment workspace before writing the diagnosis.

#!/bin/bash
# GRPO on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (verl FSDP + vLLM), sized for one GPU, with verl's full-determinism mode
# enabled as in docs/advance/determinism.md (rollout seed 42; deterministic actor and ref). vLLM 0.17's
# batch-invariant mode, which full_determinism turns on, refuses to start unless the attention backend is set
# explicitly, and torch 2.10's deterministic Inductor rejects vLLM's compile-time autotuning, so the rollout runs
# eager.
# Extra Hydra overrides given on the command line are appended last and take precedence.
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct}
DATA=${DATA:-$WS/data}
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-1}
TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-30}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-5}
BATCH=${BATCH:-64}
N_SAMPLES=${N_SAMPLES:-8}
MAX_RESPONSE=${MAX_RESPONSE:-1024}
SEED=${SEED:-1}
EXP=${EXP:-qwen25_1.5b_gsm8k_grpo_deterministic}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs}

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="$DATA/gsm8k/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="$DATA/gsm8k/test.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=$BATCH \
  data.max_prompt_length=512 \
  data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$((BATCH / 2)) \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N_SAMPLES \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=42 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.attention_backend=FLASH_ATTN \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.param_offload=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism=True \
  trainer.use_v1=False \
  trainer.critic_warmup=0 \
  trainer.logger='["console","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=gsm8k_grpo_deterministic \
  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$N_GPUS \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS \
  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations" \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=32 \
  +ray_kwargs.ray_init.object_store_memory=21474836480 \
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

    @SkipManager.annotate(role="rollout")
    async def generate_sequences(self, prompts: DataProto) -> DataProto:
        """Split input batch and dispatch to agent loop workers.

        Args:
            prompts (DataProto): Input batch.

        Returns:
            DataProto: Output batch.
        """
        # Attach per-sample priority to the batch (like ``uid``) so each sample gets
        # a globally-unique priority that flows to vLLM request scheduling. Assigned
        # before chunking so chunks own disjoint ranges without per-worker offsets.
        if "priority" not in prompts.non_tensor_batch:
            prompts.non_tensor_batch["priority"] = np.arange(len(prompts), dtype=np.int64)

        chunkes = prompts.chunk(len(self.agent_loop_workers))
        outputs = await asyncio.gather(
            *[
                worker.generate_sequences.remote(chunk)
                for worker, chunk in zip(self.agent_loop_workers, chunkes, strict=True)
            ]
        )
        output = DataProto.concat(outputs)

        # calculate performance metrics
        metrics = [output.meta_info.pop("metrics") for output in outputs]  # List[List[Dict[str, str]]]
        timing = self._performance_metrics(metrics, output)

        output.meta_info = {"timing": timing, **outputs[0].meta_info}
        return output

        timing = {}
        t_generate_sequences = np.array([metric["generate_sequences"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])

        validate (bool): whether is a validate step.

    Returns:
        list: trajectory.
    """
    trajectory_info = []
    rollout_n = 0
    for i in range(len(index)):
        if i > 0 and index[i - 1] == index[i]:
            rollout_n += 1
        else:
            rollout_n = 0
        trajectory_info.append({"step": step, "sample_index": index[i], "rollout_n": rollout_n, "validate": validate})
    return trajectory_info

# Check: after repeat(interleave=True), does each group of 8 rollouts for a prompt
# share the same priority value, making request_id identical under full_determinism?

print('Since replica_rank=0 and seed=42, ALL requests get seed=42')
print('vLLM with same (model_weights, prompt, seed) produces identical outputs')
print('Therefore all 8 rollouts of the same prompt are byte-for-byte identical')
print()
print('The request_id differs (det-0, det-8, ...) but that only affects scheduling, not sampling')
print('The sampling seed is what determines output, and it is the same for all 8 copies')

# Full Determinism for Reproducible RL Training

**Authors**: Haichuan Hu, Yongxiang Huang, Jiawei Zhang, Nguyen Long

Last updated: 06/16/2026.

## Overview

By default, RL training in verl is **not** bitwise reproducible: identical configs run twice can produce different reward curves due to nondeterminism in GPU kernels, request scheduling, hash-based routing, and batch composition. The full determinism feature closes these gaps, enabling two identical runs to produce **bitwise-aligned reward curves**.

Useful for:

- **Debugging**: reproduce a training failure exactly, step-by-step
- **Regression testing**: verify that a code change has no silent effect on training outcomes
- **Research**: ensure fair comparison when evaluating algorithmic changes

## Quick Start

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    full_determinism: true
    seed: 42
  actor:
    fsdp_config:
      full_determinism: true
  ref:
    fsdp_config:
      full_determinism: true

reward:
  reward_model:
    enable: true
    rollout:
      full_determinism: true
      seed: 42
```

Or via Hydra overrides:

```bash
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=true \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=42 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism=true \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism=true \
  reward.reward_model.enable=true \
  reward.reward_model.rollout.full_determinism=true \
  reward.reward_model.rollout.seed=42 \
  [other config overrides...]
```

> **Important:** `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be set **before the Python interpreter starts**. verl handles this automatically — it sets `PYTHONHASHSEED` from `rollout.seed` before `ray.init()` and propagates it to all Ray actors. Do NOT set it manually.

## Configuration Reference

| Parameter | Default | Scope | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism` | `false` | Rollout | Enables deterministic rollout generation |
| `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed` | `42` | Rollout | Base seed; each replica uses `replica_rank + seed` |
| `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism` | `false` | Actor | Enables deterministic PyTorch ops for actor |
| `actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism` | `false` | Ref model | Enables deterministic PyTorch ops for reference model |
| `reward.reward_model.rollout.full_determinism` | `false` | Reward model | Enables deterministic RM inference (forces `max_num_seqs=1`) |
| `reward.reward_model.rollout.seed` | `42` | Reward model | Base seed for RM vLLM server |

## How It Works

Determinism is enforced at five layers. All must be enabled for full E2E reproducibility:

### PyTorch-level

`enable_full_determinism(seed)` sets `PYTHONHASHSEED`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, `FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC`, seeds all RNGs, calls `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)`, and disables cuDNN benchmarking. Applied in all training engine implementations.

### Environment propagation

`main_ppo.run_ppo()` sets three env vars before `ray.init()`:

- `PYTHONHASHSEED` — freezes Python hash() and dict ordering
- `VERL_FULL_DETERMINISM` — signals subprocesses to apply determinism
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` — makes vLLM outputs independent of batch composition

These are forwarded to all Ray actors via `PPO_RAY_RUNTIME_ENV`.

### vLLM batch invariance + per-request seed

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` ensures vLLM outputs don't depend on which other requests are batched together. Each `generate()` call injects `SamplingParams.seed = replica_rank + config.seed` to reset RNG per request.

### Priority scheduling + deterministic routing

Without determinism, request order depends on arrival timing and server selection on dict iteration order. When `full_determinism=true`:

- Each sample gets a globally unique priority injected into the batch (`non_tensor_batch["priority"]`), so each rollout request is scheduled with a stable, distinct priority
- `SingleTurnAgentLoop` uses `request_id=f"det-{priority}"` instead of random UUID
- `GlobalRequestLoadBalancer` tie-breaking uses `hash(request_id) % len(candidates)` — deterministic with frozen `PYTHONHASHSEED`

> **Note:** `priority` is a vLLM-only parameter. `LLMServerClient.generate()` automatically filters it for non-vLLM backends.

### Reward model serialization

vLLM's `/classify` endpoint (used by RM) does not support priority or batch invariance. When `full_determinism=true`, `RewardModelManager` forces `max_num_seqs=1`, serializing RM inference one request at a time.

## Side Effects and Limitations

**Performance**: deterministic PyTorch kernels are slower, cuDNN benchmarking is disabled, and RM `max_num_seqs=1` causes severe throughput loss. Typical E2E throughput drops 10–30% without RM; RM determinism can drop significantly more.

**Recommendation**: Only enable for debugging, regression testing, or research. Leave disabled for production training.

**Nondeterministic fallbacks**: Some GPU ops have no deterministic implementation. `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)` warns when these are encountered.

**Backend support**:

| Backend | Rollout | Reward model |
|---------|---------|--------------|
| vLLM | ✅ | ✅ (serialized) |
| SGLang | ❌ | ❌ |
| TensorRT-LLM | ❌ | ❌ |

**PYTHONHASHSEED**: Must be set before process start. verl handles this automatically; manual Ray actor creation must propagate it via `runtime_env`.

**Data parallelism**: Each replica uses `replica_rank + seed`, producing different but internally reproducible outputs. Two runs with the same config produce bitwise-aligned results.

# RL Training Run Diagnosis

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY — zero learning throughout the entire run

The model did not learn. Val accuracy is frozen at **8.72 %** at every evaluation checkpoint (steps 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30). `actor/grad_norm`, `actor/loss`, `actor/pg_loss`, and `actor/kl_loss` are **exactly 0** at all 28 logged training steps. `critic/advantages/mean`, `critic/advantages/max`, and `critic/advantages/min` are all **0** at every step. Val generations at step 0, 15, and 30 are byte-for-byte identical. The run completed all 30 steps without a crash; the non-learning is silent.

---

## Root cause: fixed per-request vLLM seed collapses all n=8 rollouts of each prompt to an identical output

GRPO computes advantages by normalising rewards within the group of `n=8` rollouts for each prompt. When every rollout in a group is identical, all rewards within the group are equal, the group mean equals every individual reward, and the normalised advantage for every token is exactly **0**. A zero-advantage batch produces zero policy gradient loss, zero KL loss, zero gradient, and no weight update — regardless of whether any individual rollout received a non-zero reward (the logs confirm rewards such as 0 and 1 do appear, but always uniformly within each group).

### Causal chain

1. **`full_determinism=True` with `rollout.seed=42` is set in `run_grpo_fd.sh`** (lines 52, 57–58, 66).

2. **verl's `VLLMAsyncServer._single_generate()`** (`verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py`, line 599–600) injects a per-request seed when `full_determinism` is active:
   ```python
   if self.config.full_determinism:
       sampling_params.setdefault("seed", self.replica_rank + self.config.seed)
   ```
   Because `setdefault` is used and the caller never supplies a `seed` key, **every single request gets the same seed value**: `replica_rank (0) + config.seed (42) = 42`.

3. **The trainer repeats each prompt n=8 times** (`ray_trainer.py`, line 1454: `gen_batch.repeat(repeat_times=rollout_n, interleave=True)`). All 8 copies share the same token ids and are submitted to vLLM each with seed 42.

4. **vLLM with a fixed seed deterministically produces the same token sequence for the same (prompt, seed, weights) triple.** All 8 rollouts of every prompt therefore produce a byte-for-byte identical output. This is confirmed directly by the rollout files: at steps 1, 15, and 30, every one of the 64 prompt groups has 8 identical outputs (`all_same=64, mixed=0`), and the first group's 8 outputs are literally the same string.

5. **GRPO advantage normalisation over a constant-reward group yields zero.** With all rewards equal within a group, the group mean equals each reward, and `advantage = (r - mean) / std` is either 0/0 (undefined, clamped to 0) or 0 after the subtraction. The logged `critic/advantages` confirm this — min, mean, and max are all 0 across all steps.

6. **Zero advantages ⟹ zero policy gradient loss ⟹ zero gradients ⟹ no weight updates.** The model weights are unchanged from initialisation, so val generations are identical at every checkpoint and val accuracy never moves.

### Why the launch script's design is incompatible with GRPO

The `full_determinism` feature is designed for **reproducibility across two separate runs** — it ensures that run A and run B with the same config produce the same outputs. It does so by fixing the vLLM sampling seed to a constant per-replica value. This is correct for that purpose. However, GRPO **requires within-group diversity**: the n rollouts of a single prompt must have different outputs so that some succeed and others fail, creating a non-trivial reward signal and non-zero advantages. Using `full_determinism=True` with a single replica and a single fixed seed eliminates that diversity entirely, making GRPO inoperable.

The `rollout_corr` metrics (Pearson correlation ~0.9995–0.9996, PPL ratio ~1.0001–1.0008) show the rollout and training model distributions are nearly identical — consistent with a model that has not moved — but these are a symptom, not the cause.

---

## Summary of symptoms vs. root cause

| Observation | Classification |
|---|---|
| `actor/grad_norm = 0` at all steps | Symptom |
| `actor/pg_loss = 0` at all steps | Symptom |
| `critic/advantages` all-zero at all steps | Symptom — proximate cause of zero loss |
| Val accuracy frozen at 8.72 % for all 6 evals | Symptom |
| All 8 rollouts per prompt are byte-for-byte identical | **Proximate cause** |
| `vllm_async_server.py` injects fixed seed (replica_rank + config.seed = 42) to every request via `setdefault` | **Root cause** |
| `run_grpo_fd.sh` enables `full_determinism=True` on a single-replica GRPO run | **Configuration decision that activates the root cause** |

steps.message:
The diagnosis is written to `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md`. Here is a summary of what I found.

**Verdict: unhealthy — the model learned nothing across all 30 steps.**

Val accuracy is exactly 8.72 % at every evaluation checkpoint (steps 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30). `actor/grad_norm`, `actor/pg_loss`, and all advantage statistics are identically zero at every one of the 28 logged training steps. Val generations at steps 0, 15, and 30 are byte-for-byte identical.

**Root cause: `full_determinism=True` with a single fixed vLLM seed makes all n=8 rollouts per prompt produce the same output, collapsing GRPO advantages to zero.**

The causal chain:

1. `run_grpo_fd.sh` enables `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=True` with `seed=42` and a single GPU replica.

2. `VLLMAsyncServer._single_generate()` (in `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py:600`) calls `sampling_params.setdefault("seed", self.replica_rank + self.config.seed)`. Since `replica_rank=0` and `seed=42`, every request gets seed 42, and `setdefault` means no caller can override it.

3. The trainer repeats each of the 64 training prompts 8 times (`ray_trainer.py:1454`). Every copy gets seed 42 and the same token ids, so vLLM produces byte-for-byte identical outputs for all 8 copies. Confirmed directly: at steps 1, 15, and 30, all 64 prompt groups have zero variation among their 8 rollouts.

4. GRPO normalises rewards within each group. Uniform rewards within a group make every advantage exactly zero, which makes the policy gradient loss zero, which makes the gradient zero, so no weights update.

The `full_determinism` feature is designed to make two separate runs reproduce each other. It works by pinning sampling to a constant seed. That is incompatible with GRPO, which requires within-group diversity to produce a training signal. The non-learning is silent — no crash, no warning, just a run that executes all 30 steps without any weight change.
